doc: Build a navigation mesh from triangles, ask paths, rays and the nearest place on it, add walkers and send them, place obstacles and links, step the crowd, return to a frame, and ask what would be.

tools.name: nav.observe
tools.description: The frame, the state's hash, the mesh's tiles and polygons, how many walkers (by how they are going: idle, walking, arrived, unreachable, crossing a link, off the mesh), obstacles and links

tools.name: nav.where
tools.description: Where a walker is (or every one): its place, velocity, how it is going, its target and the corners it steers for next

walker.description: the walker's id (every one when none is given)

budget.description: every walker: the most bytes of answer; walkers are left out from the last, and `more` says how many

tools.name: nav.path
tools.description: The way between two places: its corners (those where a link begins marked), its length, whether it reaches the place asked or ends as near as it can, and how many polygons it crosses

tools.name: nav.nearest
tools.description: The nearest place on the mesh to a place, within a reach

reach.description: [x, y, z], how far to look each way (2, 4, 2 when none is given)

tools.name: nav.ray
tools.description: A straight walk along the mesh: whether it gets there, how far it goes and the wall's normal where it stops

tools.name: nav.build
tools.description: The mesh built anew from triangles for one size of walker; the obstacles, links and walkers of the old one go
tools.undo: nav.seek to the frame before it

corners.description: [i, j, k, …], three indices of points a triangle

radius.description: the walker's radius (0.4 m when none is given)

climb.description: the highest step it climbs (0.4 m)

slope.description: the steepest slope it walks, radians (0.785: 45°)

tools.name: nav.add
tools.description: A walker of the crowd, at the nearest place on the mesh to `at`
tools.undo: nav.remove, or nav.seek to the frame before it

tools.name: nav.remove
tools.description: A walker taken out of the crowd
tools.undo: nav.seek to the frame before it

tools.name: nav.target
tools.description: A walker sent to the nearest place on the mesh to `to`, its path planned whole now (or stopped, with no `to`)
tools.undo: nav.seek to the frame before it

then.why: step the crowd: it walks from the next step

to.description: [x, y, z]; none: stop where it is

tools.name: nav.obstacle
tools.description: An obstacle placed (a cylinder or a box) or taken away (`remove`): the tiles under it are built again, and walkers whose way it crosses plan again
tools.undo: nav.obstacle with `remove`, or nav.seek to the frame before it

then.why: see whether the way is still open

shape.description: cylinder (the default: `at` its base) or box (`at` its centre)

half.description: box: [x, y, z], its half extents

tools.name: nav.link
tools.description: Two places joined that a walker could not walk between (a jump, a ladder), or a link taken away (`remove`): the tile where it starts is built again
tools.undo: nav.link with `remove`, or nav.seek to the frame before it

radius.description: how near the mesh each end is (0.5 m)

both_ways.description: a boolean (its id): true when none is given

tools.name: nav.step
tools.description: Steps the crowd: every walker steered along its corridor, kept apart, moved on the mesh, carried across a link
tools.undo: nav.seek to the frame it began at

steps.description: how many (1 when none is given)

tools.name: nav.seek
tools.description: Returns to a frame within the history kept, bit for bit (a checkpoint and the inputs since, given again); what is stepped from there is a new branch
tools.undo: none within the world: what came after the frame is another branch's

then.why: read the world at the frame returned to

tools.name: nav.branch
tools.description: What would be: the world some steps ahead, a walker sent somewhere first if one is given, observed as nav.observe does; the world itself untouched

steps.description: how far ahead (1 when none is given)

tasks.name: find-the-way
tasks.summary: Read the mesh, then the way between two places and how far a straight walk gets

tasks.name: send-a-walker
tasks.summary: Add a walker, send it, step the crowd and read where it got to

tasks.name: block-and-see
tasks.summary: Ask what an obstacle would do before placing it: a branch ahead, then the obstacle and the path again
